assessments.reasoning: Visual inspection of matching PDF pages 62 and 72 shows §11.8's suspension, control handoff, and assignment of the yielded expression values to the invoking for statement. Section 13.2 describes sequence items as groups of zero or more objects.

challenge.method: Compare scanned §11.8 and §13.2 with §11.7 on the same printed page. Test whether return and yield are confused and whether a yield requires a nonempty payload.
challenge.results: Return terminates the iterator and carries no iterator return values. Yield instead presents the next item while suspending the iterator. The manual allows zero objects, so yielded values means the actual payload, including an empty one.

limitations: The review concerns the documented control handoff. It does not establish a coroutine implementation, stack strategy, or nonempty payload requirement.
